speaker: Doctor
text: I see an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To start our investigation, how would you describe the nature of his vomiting, and has he passed any stool recently?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Is the vomiting projectile or forceful, and does it contain bile or look like coffee grounds? Also, are there any specific signs like an olive-shaped mass in the abdomen or blood in the stool? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Patient
text: The abdomen still looks swollen and the baby seems uncomfortable, especially in the lower abdomen. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Intestinal Malrotation with Midgut Volvulus
